text: Yolo Akili, born Michael Todd Robinson Jr on October 14, 1981, is an activist, writer, poet, counselor, and community organizer who advocates for mental and emotional health in the Black community. He is the author of *Dear Universe: Letters of Affirmation and Empowerment* and the founder and executive director of BEAM (Black Emotional and Mental Health Collective), named in honor of Joseph Beam, a cultural and political activist who inspired Akili to reflect on his personal vulnerability as a Black gay man. After graduating from Georgia State University with a degree in Women's and African American Studies, Akili adopted the name Yolo Akili. He worked as a counselor, yoga instructor, and poet, releasing a spoken word album titled *Purple Galaxy* that explores sexual identity. He joined AID Atlanta's HIV prevention team and served as a life support counselor at National AIDS & Education Services to Minorities (NAESM), and co-founded Sweet Tea: Southern Queer Men's Collective with Charles Stephens, a group dedicated to combating sexism among queer pro-feminist men. As the regional training coordinator for Men Stopping Violence (MSV), Akili developed batterer intervention programs to educate heterosexual African American men in their 40s about abetting violence and sexism against women. Writing for Shondaland, Akili detailed his personal struggle with domestic violence, the shame faced by LGBTQ+ individuals in abusive relationships, and the need for trauma survivors to avoid normalizing destructive behavior. He observed institutional barriers preventing Black people from accessing emotional healthcare, including a case in Atlanta where an HIV-testing counselor failed to connect a patient with care. In response, Akili founded BEAM to remove barriers to mental health care access for Black people, emphasizing the need for training community members—from grocery clerks to aunties to barbers—to provide emotional support where licensed professionals are absent. Through BEAM, Akili sponsors community events that teach emotional recognition, self-care, and access to trauma support, and provides grants to mental health organizations serving marginalized communities. BEAM’s outreach has included panels with notable figures such as Jenifer Lewis, Raquel Willis, Patrisse Cullors, Vanessa Baden, Dr. Consuela Ward, Dr. Moya Bailley, Tre'Vell Andeson, James Bland, Nathan Hale Williams, Grant Emerson Harvey, Darryl Stephens, and Aaryn Lang. Akili is a feminist advocate who denounces misogyny in the gay community, rejects the notion that gay men have agency to fondle women’s bodies, promotes therapy over self-medication, and affirms that "healing is our birthright," while challenging HIV/AIDS-related trauma and stigma. In 2015, he helped lead a study at the Children's Hospital of Los Angeles on improving HIV treatment among young Black and Latino men (HYM). His writing has appeared in TheBody.com, Essence, Everyday Feminism, The Atlanta Journal Constitution, Cassius, and Shondaland, and on HuffPost, where he challenged power dynamics in same-gender relationships, rejected the narrative that Black people are deficient in every way, and called for ending partner violence as a priority in a Black (feminist) future where gendered socialization is declared a public health emergency. He has delivered keynotes and panels at events including the National African American MSM Leadership Conference, Claremont McKenna College, AIDS United, Vanderbilt University, Ramapo College, Harvard University, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, Clayton State University, Baruch College, Agnes Scott College, Fordham University, Northern Illinois University, and Columbia University. In 2009, he received the Creative Leadership Award from the Feminist Women's Health Center; in 2013, after releasing *Dear Universe*, he was named a "Health Hero" by BET; in 2016, he appeared on NBC News’ *Back to Reality* podcast; in 2018, he was recognized by Blavity as one of "28 Young Black Creators And Leaders Making History Today"; that same year, he was nominated by AIDS United for the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation Health Equity Award, which he received, and was named a "Health Equity Hero" by TheBody.com; in 2019, Essence Magazine featured him in their Black History Month coverage for his work in the Black LGBTQ+ community; on June 10, 2020, Jordan Peele donated $1 million to five Black Lives Matter organizations through MonkeyPaw Productions, with $200,000 going to Akili and BEAM; that month, Well's Fargo Bank awarded Akili and BEAM $25,000 at BET’s 2020 Music Awards.
